---
title: "Sparse log-concave NMF"
description: "Recover compound profiles and spectra with local likelihood updates and a parsimonious rank."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

`splogconNMF()` extends sparse deconvolution to compounds whose profiles are
broader or more asymmetric than the point spread function. It combines an
initial grouped `L0glm.fit()` with fast spectral fusion and local constrained
updates. Every compound has a nonnegative spectrum and a log-concave elution
profile. A low-dimensional spline basis absorbs the smooth background.

```r
fit <- splogconNMF(X, Y, background = B, family = poisson("identity"),
                  precluster = 32L)
fit$rank                  # number of compounds
fit$H                     # sparse, unit-sum profiles
coef(fit)                 # spectra in every original channel
fitted(fit)               # profiles x spectra + background + offset
GIC(fit)
```

For experimental GC/MS intensities, `family=quasipoisson("identity")` allows
extra variation through one pooled temporal dispersion estimate. Gaussian,
negative-binomial and Gamma likelihoods are also available. The help page
[`?splogconNMF`](../reference/splogconNMF.html) gives all arguments and examples.
The [GC/MS deconvolution tutorial](gcms-deconvolution.html) shows complete
experimental examples, including CDF input, MSP export and all four plot types.

## Model and criterion

For scans \(i\), channels \(j\) and compounds \(r\),

\[
\mu_{ij}=\sum_{r=1}^K H_{ir}S_{rj}+(BA)_{ij}+O_{ij},\qquad H,S,A\geq0.
\]

The columns of \(H\) have unit sum, contiguous support and
\(\Delta^2\log H_{\cdot r}\leq0\). Spectra \(S\) therefore have the
interpretation of integrated channel intensities. The objective is

\[
J=-2\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\ell(y_{ij};\mu_{ij},\nu)+\lambda_R K,
\qquad \lambda_R=m\kappa\lambda_{IC}.
\]

Here \(m\) is the original channel count, \(\nu\) contains pooled noise
parameters and \(\kappa=1\) for independent observations. Numeric `lambda`
specifies the total compound penalty before the optional covariance adjustment.
Background coefficients and profile complexity have no additional penalty.
The original channel count is retained in this penalty when the observations
are aggregated, so changing the number of outcome groups does not change
the compound penalty.
Dividing by the channel count gives the equivalent criterion
\(-2\ell/m+\kappa\lambda_{IC}K\), with one rank penalty per compound.
The reported IC methods use the compound-count convention \(mK\), plus any
estimated shared noise parameters.

## Generalized matrix factorization

The broad statistical setting is **generalized matrix factorization (GMF)**:
an exponential-family mean is linked to a low-rank product, optionally with
observed covariate effects and offsets. See
[Kidziński et al. (2022)](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v23/20-1104.html) and
[Castiglione et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxag010).
For example, the latter mean-model structure is

\[
g(\mu)=X_{\rm row}B_{\rm row}^{\top}
       +B_{\rm col}X_{\rm col}^{\top}+UV^{\top}+O.
\]

Our model uses the identity link, \(U=H\), \(V^{\top}=S\), and
\(X_{\rm row}=B\), \(B_{\rm row}^{\top}=A\) for the smooth background;
the column-covariate term is omitted. It adds nonnegativity, unit-area
log-concave profiles and a compound-count penalty to select the rank.
Thus **sparse log-concave nonnegative GMF** describes the model, while the
function retains the familiar `splogconNMF()` name.

## Deviance matrix factorization and Bregman NMF

`splogconNMF()` is a **rank-penalized, nonnegative deviance matrix
factorization with log-concave profiles**. It belongs to the deviance-based
framework of [Wang & Carvalho (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1214/23-EJS2174),
using an identity link for the additive mean \(\mu=HS+BA+O\).
The loss also connects directly to
[NMF with Bregman divergences](https://doi.org/10.3390/s23167229).

For a regular exponential-dispersion model with fixed noise parameters,

\[
\ell(y;\theta,\phi)=\frac{y\theta-b(\theta)}{\phi}+c(y,\phi),
\qquad \mu=b'(\theta),
\]

let \(\Psi=b^*\) be the convex conjugate of \(b\). Its Bregman divergence is

\[
D_\Psi(y,\mu)=\Psi(y)-\Psi(\mu)-\Psi'(\mu)(y-\mu).
\]

Since \(\Psi'(\mu)=\theta(\mu)\) and
\(\Psi(\mu)=\mu\theta(\mu)-b\{\theta(\mu)\}\), substitution gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
D_\Psi(y,\mu)
&=y\theta(y)-b\{\theta(y)\}-y\theta(\mu)+b\{\theta(\mu)\},\\
2\{\ell(y;y,\phi)-\ell(y;\mu,\phi)\}
&=\frac{2}{\phi}D_\Psi(y,\mu).
\end{aligned}
\]

Here the likelihood on the second line is written in mean coordinates.
Boundary observations use the corresponding limits. Thus, conditional on the
noise parameters, fitting is equivalent to minimizing

\[
2\sum_{ij}\frac{w_{ij}}{\phi}D_\Psi(y_{ij},(HS+BA+O)_{ij})
   +\lambda_RK
\]

under the nonnegativity, profile-normalization and log-concavity constraints.
The saturated likelihood contributes a constant in these conditional model
comparisons. The corresponding divergences include:

| Noise model | Generator \(\Psi(u)\) | Half unit deviance \(D_\Psi(y,\mu)\) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Gaussian | \(u^2/2\) | \((y-\mu)^2/2\) |
| Poisson | \(u\log u-u\) | \(y\log(y/\mu)-y+\mu\) |
| Gamma, uncensored \(y>0\) | \(-\log u\) | \(y/\mu-\log(y/\mu)-1\) |
| NB2, fixed shape \(\theta\) | \(u\log u-(u+\theta)\log(u+\theta)\) | \(y\log(y/\mu)-(y+\theta)\log\{(y+\theta)/(\mu+\theta)\}\) |

For NB2, \(\phi=1\) and the shape \(\theta\) enters the generator.
Gaussian, Poisson and Gamma therefore give squared-error, generalized KL and
Itakura–Saito NMF losses. Quasipoisson gives the KL kernel scaled by its
dispersion. Censored Gamma and the mean-dependent-shape extensions use their
full likelihood kernels described below; estimated noise parameters are
compared using the full likelihood as well.

## From a chromatogram to NIST spectra

`GCMSdeco()` connects the factorization to ANDI-MS `.cdf` files and NIST `.msp`
spectral libraries:

```r
fit <- GCMSdeco("beer.cdf", "beer.msp", alkanes_file="alkanes.cdf",
                time_range=c(6, Inf))
fit$compounds
coef(fit)                 # spectra in all original mass channels
GIC(fit)
```

Choose `time_range` to match the acquisition's solvent delay or the window of
interest. The default workflow uses ten overlapping blind-PSF windows,
size-adjusted aggregation to at most 32 outcome groups, and a low-df spline
background. Alkane peaks provide an optional calibrated PSF start. Final
refinement and exported spectra retain every original mass channel.

For instrumental intensities the default quasipoisson model estimates one
shared dispersion. Its variance scale also sets the working precision of the
total-ion PSF pilot. The final likelihood uses the original channels and the
same frozen noise parameters. [The reference page](../reference/GCMSdeco.html)
details the working-weight formula, automatic spline dimension, retention-time
units and exported metadata.

## Local quadratic updates

For a coefficient \(b\geq0\), keep the rest of the signal in an offset
\(r_i\) and write \(\mu_i=r_i+x_i b\). With negative log-likelihood score
\(g_i\) and positive working curvature \(I_i\), propose

\[
b^+=\max\left\{0,b-\frac{\sum_i w_i x_i g_i}
{\sum_i w_i x_i^2 I_i}\right\}.
\]

Actual-loss backtracking and a zero-boundary check complete each scalar solve.
The Poisson branch uses a faster bracketed likelihood solve. Its score
\(\sum_iw_ix_i(1-y_i/\mu_i)\) is monotone, and its nonnegative root is bounded
above by \(\sum_iw_iy_i/\sum_iw_ix_i\). Channels are independent conditional on
the profiles, allowing deterministic OpenMP parallelism.

Local profile updates use the original observation likelihood. For
\(\eta_i=\log h_i\), \(\mu_{ij}=r_{ij}+h_i s_j\), the chain-rule score and
working information are

\[
g_{\eta,i}=h_i\sum_jw_{ij}s_jg_{\mu,ij},\qquad
I_{\eta,i}=h_i^2\sum_jw_{ij}s_j^2I_{\mu,ij}.
\]

The working target is \(\eta_i-g_{\eta,i}/I_{\eta,i}\), with tiny stabilization
where the information vanishes. This quadratic approximation updates the
**log profile parameters**; the observed intensities remain on their original
scale and acceptance uses their actual likelihood.

A smooth concave log profile can be written as

\[
\eta(t)=a+bt-\frac12\sum_j c_j
  \{(t-u_j)_+^2-(t-v_j)_+^2\},\qquad c_j\geq0,
\]

where the intervals \([u_j,v_j)\) partition the local time window. Its second
derivative is \(-\sum_jc_j\mathbf1_{[u_j,v_j)}(t)\leq0\), giving hard
log-concavity. The intercept and slope are unrestricted, and a small
nonnegative quadratic solve estimates the curvature coefficients. For more
detailed local adjustments, piecewise-linear log-profile increments preserve
the existing fine-scale curvature; a concave-envelope projection removes
numerical constraint residuals. Backtracking between feasible log profiles
preserves concavity and accepts only likelihood improvements.

Fusion starts with spectral compatibility and profile overlap. Broad-anchor
and contained-tail proposals are refined only within the affected windows;
other compounds remain in an offset. The full original-channel criterion
decides whether each proposed rank change is retained. A final conservative
pass can reunite broad profiles with complementary ion sets when their
profile cosine is at least 0.95. Neighbouring modes are guarded during its
local refit. `control=list(profile_cycles=0L)` disables the main shape-refinement
stage; `control=list(profile_fusion=FALSE)` disables the final conservative pass.

| Noise model | Variance | Negative log-likelihood score in the mean |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Gaussian | \(\phi\) | \((\mu-y)/\phi\) |
| Poisson | \(\mu\) | \(1-y/\mu\) |
| Quasipoisson | \(\phi\mu\) | \((1-y/\mu)/\phi\) |
| NB2 | \(\mu+\mu^2/\theta\) | \(\theta(\mu-y)/\{\mu(\mu+\theta)\}\) |
| Gamma | \(\phi\mu^2\) | \((\mu-y)/(\phi\mu^2)\) |
| NB1 | \(\phi\mu\) | \(\{\psi(a)-\psi(a+y)+\log\phi\}/(\phi-1)\), \(a=\mu/(\phi-1)\) |
| Common-scale Gamma | \(b_0\mu\) | \(\{\psi(\mu/b_0)+\log b_0-\log y\}/b_0\) |

The final two models use the exact distributions documented in
[`signal_families`](../reference/signal_families.html). Their observed positive
curvatures are differences of trigamma functions for NB1 and
\(\psi_1(\mu/b_0)/b_0^2\) for common-scale Gamma. The latter is convex in the
mean; the NB1 curvature is nonnegative because trigamma decreases on the
positive real line.

## Censored Gamma intensities

Recorded zeros may represent intensities below a detection limit \(d\), whose
contribution is \(\log P(Y<d;\mu)\). Positive observations contribute their
ordinary density. For standard Gamma, set \(a=1/\phi\),
\(z=d/(\phi\mu)\); its negative log-CDF derivative is

\[
g(\mu)=\frac{z^a e^{-z}}{\Gamma(a)P(a,z)\mu}.
\]

For common-scale Gamma, \(z=d/b_0\) stays fixed and \(a=\mu/b_0\) changes.
The convergent incomplete-Gamma series

\[
P(a,z)=\frac{e^{-z}z^a}{\Gamma(a+1)}
\left\{1+\sum_{k\geq1}\frac{z^k}{(a+1)\cdots(a+k)}\right\}
\]

provides its shape derivative when \(z\) is small. The general branch uses the
Gamma CDF and a numerical shape derivative. Both branches are checked against
the actual censored likelihood. The default detection limit is 0.5 intensity
units and can be changed through `control$censor`.

## Fusion, aggregation and rank selection

1. Obtain a variance-matched grouped deconvolution start, retaining the spline
   background as compulsory unpenalized terms.
2. Compare normalized spectra by Jensen--Shannon information loss. Propose
   fusions when their elution profiles overlap and their combined profile can
   be made log-concave. Clustering itself performs no regression fits.
3. Refine each proposal locally, holding all outside contributions fixed.
   Overlapping spectra and the candidate profile can adjust together.
4. Accept a rank change when
   \(-2(\ell_{new}-\ell_{old})+\lambda_R(K_{new}-K_{old})\leq0\).
5. Update broad profiles, smooth background coefficients and spectra, followed
   by final boundary checks and rank pruning.

Algebraic fusion uses a least concave majorant of the log profile, followed
by normalization. Local likelihood updates impose hard concavity constraints
in their quadratic solves. Every complete accepted stage decreases the actual
criterion, within numerical tolerance. `history` and `ledger_error` make this
property directly checkable.

With `precluster=32L`, the initial workflow uses at most 32 aggregated outcome
groups. Size factors `colSums(pmax(Y,0))` account for different total ion
intensities. Final refinement returns to every original channel. Independent
NB1 variables sharing \(p=1/\phi\) are closed under sums, because their
probability-generating functions multiply as

\[
\prod_j\left\{\frac{p}{1-(1-p)t}\right\}^{\mu_j/(\phi-1)}
=\left\{\frac{p}{1-(1-p)t}\right\}^{\sum_j\mu_j/(\phi-1)}.
\]

The same property holds for common-scale Gamma latent signals, through
\(\prod_j(1+b_0t)^{-\mu_j/b_0}=(1+b_0t)^{-\sum_j\mu_j/b_0}\).
Standard NB2 and Gamma use moment matching in the reduced problem. Censoring
or different channel weights also give working aggregate approximations;
final scoring always uses the original responses and their specified model.

## Temporal variation

High-order differences suppress the slowly varying mean. With
\(a_k=(-1)^k{r\choose k}\) and stationary covariance \(c_h\),

\[
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\Delta^r e)}{{2r\choose r}}
=c_0+2\sum_{h=1}^r(-1)^h
\frac{{2r\choose r+h}}{{2r\choose r}}c_h.
\]

The identity follows by expanding the variance and using
\(\sum_k a_k a_{k+h}=(-1)^h{2r\choose r+h}\). With lag-one covariance this
reduces to \(c_0-2r c_1/(r+1)\). Fourth and eighth differences estimate the
marginal variance and lag-one covariance. The optional penalty multiplier
\(\kappa=1+2\widehat\rho_1\) approximates the local information loss for
smooth directions, while the marginal scale stays in the component likelihood.
This is a scalar working covariance adjustment. Composite-likelihood theory
relates the broader correction to \(\operatorname{tr}(JH^{-1})\), where \(H\)
is sensitivity and \(J\) is score covariance (Varin, Reid & Firth, 2011).

and [Gamma](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/GammaDist.html)
parameterizations. The compound-count criterion, local log-concave fusion and
their integration with L0glm's grouped initialization are developments of this
package.
